findings.message: The new PM notification rules (allocations.over-capacity when {over:true}, allocations.changed when {over:false}) and the monthSettled clears depend on the extra payload fields: over, personUserId, project, month, total and byUser. Only the month-by-month branch of setAllocation fills them in. The standing branch still returns an AllocationSet that has none of these fields and emits no monthSettled. A previous round reported this, and it is still open. Build the same load, over and settled events in the standing branch, and add a variant test that covers month, range and standing.
findings.scenario: Someone else sets Kasun to 80% on CON until further notice while he is already at 60% elsewhere. The payload has no `over` field, so neither rule matches. The PM gets no notification, and an earlier over-capacity notification is never cleared.

findings.message: 'Over' is defined two ways. The UI (conflictsOf, overFlags, the Lane frame, the Fix chip) and get_over_allocation compare the total to the person's capacity (HR FTE). overLines/overCheck, loadOf (the notification `over` flag and settled months) and stillOver use a fixed threshold of 100. For anyone not at 1.0 FTE, the two disagree. Use one helper that compares against capacity.
findings.scenario: Someone at 0.5 FTE is allocated 80%. The board shows them red with a Fix chip. allocate makes the card without asking 'Are you sure?', no over-capacity notification fires, the month is emitted as 'settled', and stillOver drops the check's suggestion.

findings.message: The over-100% 'Are you sure?' gate was added to allocate's propose but not to allocate_only. allocate_only's propose runs only scopeCheck, and its percent goes up to 200, so the same over-allocation reaches a card without the question or an overOk round trip. Call overCheck (and overNote) from allocate_only too.
findings.scenario: "Put Kasun only on CON at 150% in December" → allocate_only makes the card straight away. The check that 'allocate' enforces is never asked.

findings.message: The grid now shows six months, and the pulse and list_allocations descriptions were updated to say so. get_load_summary's description still says 'Per month (the five shown)', while loadSummary returns one row per grid month (six). A previous round reported this exact second copy. Derive the number from the window, or say six.
findings.scenario: A user asks "how loaded are we?". The tool description tells the model five months are shown, but the result has six rows, and the chat rules say six. The model reports five months or drops the sixth.

findings.message: allocationCards ignores its month and today arguments and builds the capacity and allocation window from the real clock (new Date()). The rest of Reports, including awayCard and the report month, uses settings.today (the pinned 'month Reports is on'). The page and the PDF then mix two clocks. Build the window from the report's month or today.
findings.scenario: Reports is on October 2026 (pinned today 2026-10-16) and the real date is 2026-11-23. The briefing and the 'Over-allocated and bench' and 'Capacity' sections cover Nov–Apr, under an October heading, while leave covers October.

findings.message: Roster people without a login are now added with userId = p.userId ?? p.id, so their person id is used as a userId. personPin then pins them as get_person_utilisation { userId: <personId> }. That tool resolves auth users, so the pin points at no record, which counts as a missing pin. The id also keys hours and titles. Give such people a pin that resolves by person id, or don't pin them through get_person_utilisation.
findings.scenario: An HR person with no account who is allocated this month appears as a 'no time yet' row. Pinning that row and asking chat returns null ('you may not see that person').

findings.message: Every other chat card action (confirmChat, cancelChat, checkCardField, takeAction) takes `as` and calls sameUser(viewer, as) to refuse a session that changed user. The new changeChat takes neither, and Chat.tsx savePercent does not pass userId. Add `as` and sameUser.
findings.scenario: Tab A is signed in as Maya with an open allocate card. In tab B, the user signs in as someone else. Pressing Update on the percent in tab A edits the card as the new viewer instead of returning SignedInElsewhere.

findings.message: The Allocation check suggestion's title and detail no longer say what accepting does. The title used to be 'Move X to N% on P in M'. Now it is 'X is at 160% in December 2026', and the detail lists the current plan. The proposed change (project and new percent) is still applied on accept. On /suggestions, the person accepts a change the screen never states. Keep the proposed change in the title or detail.
findings.scenario: A PM on /suggestions reads 'Kasun Dias is at 160% in December 2026 — Contoso 80%, Fleet 80%' and accepts. Fleet is set to 40% without the screen ever saying so.

findings.message: The conflict card (.ad-ccard) shows a person's total and month with no PinButton of its own; only the Take action AskButton carries a pin. The header stat pills (Header.tsx: 'N conflicts · Dec', 'Everyone · N people') and the runway fact chips (Runway.tsx runwayFacts) also show metrics with no PinButton. Add a PinButton to each, resolving through get_allocation or list_allocations / get_capacity_forecast.
findings.scenario: Pin the current conflict (Ayesha, 120%, December) → there is no pin control on that card.

findings.message: scopeCheck reads `auth.user` with raw SQL, and suggested.ts `told` reads `core.event` with raw SQL. The allocations module now reads schemas it does not own directly, instead of through a contract or shared package read.

Code and docs disagree. The README says the pulse shows capacity for the 'next five months' and over-allocation and bench for the 'next three months'; the code uses six for both. It still lists set_utilisation_target under 'Admin, reports:admin', but it is now reports:target and granted to PM and Leadership.
The rule hard-codes 'Six months are shown, November to April; January to April are forecast'. From December on, the model will name the wrong months. Phrase it without fixed month names.

Closing chat after a show tool call rewrites the URL to keep only `view`. On Reports, the group is in `group` (and the table in `view`), so closing chat after show_reports with group=mine silently switches the page back to the viewer's default group.

Band, Stats, ByProject, ComingUp, GroupSwitch and Trend are added or edited but no longer rendered (ReportsView doesn't use them). They are dead code, and they are a second copy of the lede and pin logic.

The 'over-allocated' rule is now written several times, and the copies disagree. The grid, board, Conflicts and overLine use totals > capacity with capacity > 0. stillOver, overCheck and checkAllocations use sum > 100 and ignore FTE. loadSummary (over) and monthOutlook use totals > capacity with no capacity > 0 guard. Fix: put one isOver(total, capacity) in one place and use it everywhere.
findings.scenario: A 0.5 FTE person planned at 80%. The board and Conflicts show them over and offer 'Fix'. allocate makes a card without asking 'Are you sure?', and list_allocation_suggestions drops their suggestion as no longer over. A leaver with capacity 0 and 20% planned is 'over' in get_load_summary and the Reports pulse, but not on the board.

findings.message: allocate's propose decides 'edited on a card' from `a.standing === undefined`. The model can send standing itself. Then the 'over 100%, ask Are you sure? first' gate that the description and chat rules promise is skipped. overcheck.ts also has a second copy of this propose logic (proposeAllocate) that nothing uses, and the two can drift apart. Fix: pass an explicit flag for the card-edit path (or check the source), and delete the unused copy.
findings.scenario: The model calls allocate {Ayesha, CON, 2026-12, 100, standing: false} → a card is made at once, and nobody is asked 'Are you sure?' about 160%.

findings.message: editAction changes only input, fields and title. The card keeps its old `lines`, `look` and over-note, and propose and note are not run again. The PercentEdit or 'make Kasun 40%' path therefore shows the old percent on the card, while Add it writes the new one. The over-100% note is also not recomputed. Fix: rebuild the card through the tool's card/propose/note for the new input, as when the card was first proposed, and test 10→40 and 10→150.
findings.scenario: Card 'Kasun, HR Insights, 10%' → the percent is edited to 150 → the card's lines still read 10% with no over note → Add it writes 150%.

findings.message: allocate_only returns `{...set}`, so its audit record keeps only the last setAllocation's `before` and `after`. The rows it cleared on other projects (their earlier percents) are missing from the audit, so the record can't show or undo what was removed. Fix: merge the cleared slots' before rows into the returned before and after.
findings.scenario: Kasun has CON 60% and FLT 40% in Dec. allocate_only {Kasun, HRI, 2026-12} → the audit before shows only HRI (none). Nothing records that CON 60 and FLT 40 were removed.

findings.message: The group only ever widens the rows. loadInputs keeps everyone with visible hours whatever the group, and the roster only adds allocated people. 'Your people' for an Admin (or for anyone whose time scope is wider than their managed projects) still lists everyone with hours, under the 'Your people' label. Fix: when group is mine, keep only people in the roster.
findings.scenario: Admin maya opens /reports?group=mine → people with hours who are not on her projects are still listed and counted in the 'Your people' figure.

findings.message: teamOf is a second copy of the team-figure rule in figures.ts utilisationOf: the counted filter, the sums and the percent. The rounding differs (Math.round to 2 dp and a bare Math.round percent here, against tidy and pct there), so a named-people or project report's team row can differ from the page. Fix: export one team function from figures.ts and use it in both places.
findings.scenario: For the same set of people, the report's team utilisation or hours can differ from the page's figure by a rounding step.

findings.message: There are two comingOf implementations: server/coming.ts, used only by the unused ComingUp.tsx, and ui/comingItems.ts. Band.tsx, Stats.tsx, ByProject.tsx, Trend.tsx, GroupSwitch.tsx and allocations' server/fix.ts are also no longer rendered or called. Delete the dead copies so they can't drift.

changeChat turns every failure that isn't a ZodError (network, database, trace) into 'That card can't be changed any more. Ask again.', which says the card is gone when it may still be open. changeChat also skips the sameUser(viewer, as) check that every other chat action makes.
findings.scenario: A database timeout during the percent edit → the user is told the card can't be changed, but it is still open.

findings.message: Take action puts the suggestion's title and detail into the model context as instructions. The detail includes user-entered `work` labels from allocation rows. Under the @amax/ai rule, untrusted text must be passed as data.

`told` decides whether to notify by reading core.event (another schema) directly. If outbox rows are pruned, an existing suggestion is notified again. If they are kept, a person who goes over again for the same suggestion is never notified again. Keep the 'notified' state in allocations' own schema.
The README still lists set_utilisation_target as Admin-only (`reports:admin`). It now needs `reports:target`, granted to PM and Leadership.
The renderer silently deletes ' of 100%' from model text, which can change what a sentence means. Leave this rule in the prompt instead of rewriting the output.
findings.scenario: 'Kasun is at 80% of 100% capacity' is shown as 'Kasun is at 80% capacity'.
